factual_methodological.summary: Lead figures checked against same-day ISM, Eurostat and EIA releases; diffusion index, unemployment rates and physical energy flows are kept dimensionally separate.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Finding-led bilingual brief with explicit limitations and no investment recommendation.

novelty_against_previous_daily.summary: Lead evidence changes from 30 September China/Australia/UK releases to 1 October U.S. manufacturing, euro-area labour and U.S. energy trade.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 Markdown table + 1 explicit line chart + 1 causal flow per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Visuals are reproducible from cited evidence and semantically equivalent across locales.

political_neutrality.summary: No political actor or policy choice is endorsed, opposed, scored or ranked.

contrary_evidence: The U.S. manufacturing PMI edged down 0.1 point from August, so the release indicates continuity rather than acceleration.
Euro-area unemployment was unchanged month on month, so the annual increase is a marginal softening signal rather than evidence of abrupt labour-market deterioration.
limitations: PMI is a diffusion index, not a manufacturing-output growth rate.
Unemployment data refer to August and therefore lag the October publication date.
Propane export data cover the first half of 2026 and describe a structural trade channel rather than same-day demand.
notes: Approved after same-day source check, bilingual parity review and visual-semantic validation.

en.title: Global Macro — U.S. manufacturing holds expansion while Europe’s labour market softens at the margin
en.deck: U.S. manufacturing remained expansionary in September while euro-area unemployment was stable monthly but slightly higher year on year and U.S. propane exports reached record territory.
en.regime: Uneven global resilience: U.S. manufacturing remains expansionary while European labour conditions soften marginally and U.S. energy exports continue to reshape trade flows.
en.key_risk: Persistent divergence across manufacturing, labour and energy can produce different policy and market transmission across regions.
